In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the characteristic minimal value of the discontinuities of the isotropic-nematic and isotropic-smectic-A transitions in nCBs does exist.
the I–N and I–SmA phase transition in nCBs are of first order, with the discontinuity in the transition temperature being a unique characteristic of the given nCB.
the discontinuity of I–N and I–SmA transitions in rod-like nCBs exists, is finite and has a characteristic value, which is different for each nCB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new, ‘universal’ characteristic value of ΔT for the isotropic–liquid crystalline mesophase transitions in the series of nCBs has been revealed.
the characteristic value of ΔT for n-cyanobiphyls does not exist.
the ‘melting’ of liquid crystals is a continuous process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the I–N and I–SmA transition temperatures in n-alkylcynobiphenyl liquid crystals can be controlled in a wide temperature range by applying pressure and electric fields.
